prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1499; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the left lane on a Katy, Texas roadway when the vehicle collided head-on with a northbound sedan operated by Driver 2. Both vehicles sustained front-end damage consistent with a low-speed impact, and the damage pattern matches the force described by the drivers at the scene. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back and said the force of the impact pressed them firmly into the seat, which is consistent with the mechanism of the collision. Passenger was seated in the front right position and was observed exiting the vehicle with no visible difficulty, confirming their presence in the car at the time of the crash. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred exactly as Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses, who were stopped at a nearby signal, gave statements that agreed with that account. Scene photographs were taken and reviewed. Officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
